definition: Parity learning is a problem in machine learning.
details: An algorithm that solves this problem must find a function ƒ, given some samples (x, ƒ(x)) and the assurance that ƒ computes the parity of bits at some fixed locations. The samples are generated using some distribution over the input. The problem is easy to solve using Gaussian elimination provided that a sufficient number of samples (from a distribution which is not too skewed) are provided to the algorithm.

explainer.lead: Parity learning is the machine learning problem of recovering a function that computes the parity of bits at fixed but unknown locations from samples. It is easy under the right conditions, which makes it a clean test of what an algorithm can learn from limited data.

tiers.eli5: Someone hides which switches feed a light that turns on when an odd number of them are up, and you must find those switches from examples.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers treat parity as a stress test for learning algorithms and a way to probe sample efficiency. A pitfall is skewed sample distributions, since guarantees hold only when enough samples come from a distribution that is not too skewed.
tiers.paperLevel: Given samples (x, f(x)) drawn from some distribution over inputs, an algorithm must find f, which computes the parity of bits at some fixed locations. The problem is easy to solve with Gaussian elimination given enough samples from a distribution that is not too skewed.

explainer.example: With samples over three-bit inputs, Gaussian elimination over the samples recovers that f returns the parity of the first and third bits.
